extensionDescription.message: Shows psychological manipulation techniques when opening an email

introDesc1.message: 20 everyday situations. Answer instinctively — there are no right or wrong answers.

introDesc2.message: Your answers will calibrate the detector to your psychological profile.

introAttention.message: This is not a conventional anti-phishing tool. It detects psychological manipulation techniques (the APPÂT method) in your emails to help you recognise them and keep your critical thinking.

btnSkip.message: I don't want a personalized profile

skipNote.message: The detector will use maximum sensitivity for every technique.

resultDesc1.message: Your answers have calibrated the detector.

resultDesc2.message: It will now adjust its alerts to your sensitivity to each technique.

q1Text.message: You walk past a shop window that has been redecorated with warm lighting. You feel a sudden urge to go in that you didn't have yesterday.

q1AnswerA.message: I go in — the atmosphere gave me an impulse I hadn't anticipated.

q1AnswerB.message: I notice the change, but it isn't enough to make me go in.

q1AnswerC.message: I wonder why the display was changed before I act.

q1AnswerD.message: The lighting doesn't influence me; I keep walking.

q2Text.message: A colleague uses their usual tone but asks you to access a confidential file to "do them a quick favour".

q2AnswerA.message: The familiar tone puts me at ease; I help without asking questions.

q2AnswerB.message: The tone seems familiar, but I ask why they need this now.

q2AnswerC.message: I find the request unusual despite the familiar tone, and I question it.

q2AnswerD.message: I never rely on tone to judge whether a request is legitimate.

q3Text.message: A presenter shows an evocative photo and tells the story of a fictional employee who "fell for it", in an unusually dramatic tone.

q3AnswerA.message: The story moves me deeply, and I carefully memorise every piece of advice given afterwards.

q3AnswerB.message: The story makes me think, but I stay critical of the advice offered.

q3AnswerC.message: Such a dramatic staging for an internal training session seems excessive to me.

q3AnswerD.message: I'm not receptive to this kind of story; I only retain the facts.

q4Text.message: You're reading a gripping article online. A perfectly integrated pop-up offers to "continue reading in premium mode" with one click.

q4AnswerA.message: Caught up in the article, I click almost reflexively so as not to lose the thread.

q4AnswerB.message: I finish what I'm reading before considering clicking anything.

q4AnswerC.message: A pop-up that blends in that well alerts me rather than attracting me.

q4AnswerD.message: I always close this kind of pop-up without reading it.

q5Text.message: Your access badge stops working. A colleague jokes: "Looks like a big round of contract cuts…"

q5AnswerA.message: That one remark puts me on edge for the rest of the day.

q5AnswerB.message: I'm a bit shaken, but I go straight to reception to ask what's going on.

q5AnswerC.message: I take the remark for what it is — a joke — and don't think about it again.

q5AnswerD.message: That kind of rumour never affects me; I carry on with my day as normal.

q6Text.message: Your manager messages you: "We need to talk about your last report. Come see me as soon as you can." Nothing else.

q6AnswerA.message: I immediately feel awful and imagine the worst until we talk.

q6AnswerB.message: I'm worried, but I finish my current task before going.

q6AnswerC.message: The message is brief, but that means nothing in itself; I'll go at a quiet moment.

q6AnswerD.message: I don't worry about such a vague message; I'll go when I have time.

q7Text.message: During a quality review, your supervisor leafs through your file in silence, face closed, then says "We'll look at this later."

q7AnswerA.message: The silence and their expression make me anxious; I replay my whole file in my head.

q7AnswerB.message: I'm a little worried, but I wait for concrete feedback before reacting.

q7AnswerC.message: I draw no conclusions from a facial expression or a silence.

q7AnswerD.message: That kind of reaction doesn't worry me; I know the quality of my work.

q8Text.message: An email tells you your report "contains inconsistencies requiring verification via the attached portal", without saying which.

q8AnswerA.message: I panic at the thought of having got it wrong and click straight away to check.

q8AnswerB.message: I'm worried, but I contact the relevant department directly to find out more.

q8AnswerC.message: I re-read my original file before reacting to the email.

q8AnswerD.message: Without a specific detail about the error, I don't feel concerned.

q9Text.message: At a leaving party, the collection envelope goes round and everyone puts in the same amount without any prior discussion.

q9AnswerA.message: I give the same amount as everyone else without asking — it must be the norm.

q9AnswerB.message: I give an amount, but I quietly ask whether that's the usual one.

q9AnswerC.message: I give what I want, regardless of what others put in.

q9AnswerD.message: Group behaviour never influences me on this kind of personal decision.

q10Text.message: A new security procedure is announced in a meeting. The explanation is confusing, but your colleagues nod and take notes without asking anything.

q10AnswerA.message: I do the same — if they look like they understand, it must be clear.

q10AnswerB.message: I take notes too, but I plan to ask for clarification after the meeting.

q10AnswerC.message: I ask my question in the meeting, regardless of whether others seem to understand.

q10AnswerD.message: Other people's behaviour doesn't change my own need for clarity.

q11Text.message: You're explaining a method to a new colleague who stares at you coldly and frowns slightly without saying anything.

q11AnswerA.message: Their reaction throws me off and I immediately adjust how I explain.

q11AnswerB.message: I notice their reaction, but I finish my explanation as planned.

q11AnswerC.message: Their expression tells me nothing specific; I carry on without worrying.

q11AnswerD.message: I ask them directly what's wrong rather than guessing.

q12Text.message: A company-wide email from management asks for quick action, noting that "all the colleagues concerned have already confirmed".

q12AnswerA.message: The idea that everyone has already replied pushes me to do the same without waiting.

q12AnswerB.message: I reply, but first I check with a colleague whether that's actually true.

q12AnswerC.message: That claim doesn't change how I handle the request.

q12AnswerD.message: That kind of detail actually makes me more suspicious of the request.

q13Text.message: Your doctor prescribes a treatment without explanation and cuts your questions short: "Trust me, this is what I do."

q13AnswerA.message: I respect their position and follow the treatment without pressing my questions.

q13AnswerB.message: I follow the treatment, but I look up information myself afterwards.

q13AnswerC.message: I politely insist on at least a minimal explanation.

q13AnswerD.message: I get a second medical opinion before starting an unexplained treatment.

q14Text.message: A junior colleague criticises a procedure. Your supervisor replies: "With experience you understand — for now, just follow them."

q14AnswerA.message: That answer seems fair to me; better to comply until I understand.

q14AnswerB.message: I comply while saving my questions for later.

q14AnswerC.message: I think the criticism deserved a real answer, not just an appeal to seniority.

q14AnswerD.message: I'd rather back the colleague who raised the question.

q15Text.message: A trainer states: "There are two kinds of people: those who follow the rules, and those who end up causing an incident."

q15AnswerA.message: I clearly want to be in the first category, so I follow the rules without questioning them.

q15AnswerB.message: The message motivates me to be careful, but I stay critical of the rules themselves.

q15AnswerC.message: Splitting people into two categories like that seems far too simplistic to me.

q15AnswerD.message: That kind of guilt-tripping talk doesn't influence my decisions.

q16Text.message: An email from management: "It's better to follow decisions made at the top without trying to understand everything — click here to confirm your agreement."

q16AnswerA.message: That view seems realistic to me; I click to confirm without looking for more detail.

q16AnswerB.message: I click, but afterwards I ask for an explanation of this new policy.

q16AnswerC.message: I find that argument insufficient to justify acting without understanding.

q16AnswerD.message: I verify the email's authenticity before clicking anything.

q17Text.message: At a market, a seller offers: "If you buy 3 items instead of 1, I'll give you a price that's really worth it — today only."

q17AnswerA.message: The prospect of saving money motivates me to buy more than planned.

q17AnswerB.message: I'm interested, but I work out whether I actually need the extra items.

q17AnswerC.message: A same-day-only offer doesn't particularly influence me.

q17AnswerD.message: I only buy what I came for, regardless of the price.

q18Text.message: A friend offers an investment that pays back within 3 months, versus a conventional placement over several years for an equivalent gain.

q18AnswerA.message: The faster return seems clearly preferable to me; I'm tempted to accept quickly.

q18AnswerB.message: I'm tempted, but I ask for time to think before committing.

q18AnswerC.message: The speed of the return doesn't convince me without more guarantees.

q18AnswerD.message: I always prefer the safety of a conventional placement, even a slower one.

q19Text.message: At an event, someone offers to get you into a VIP area without a badge by following them through a side entrance they know.

q19AnswerA.message: The opportunity is too tempting; I follow them without thinking much.

q19AnswerB.message: I'm tempted, but I hold back thinking about the possible consequences.

q19AnswerC.message: That kind of workaround doesn't interest me, even when the opportunity arises.

q19AnswerD.message: I refuse and report the situation on principle.

q20Text.message: An email offers loyalty points in exchange for sharing your details on a partner site, with a counter showing an offer that expires in 10 minutes.

q20AnswerA.message: The quick reward and the countdown push me to act without thinking further.

q20AnswerB.message: I'm drawn to the reward, but I take the time to check the partner site.

q20AnswerC.message: Such a short countdown strikes me as a pressure tactic.

q20AnswerD.message: I'm not motivated by that kind of minor reward.
